en: Therīgāthā 5.6 Pañcakanipāta Mittākāḷītherīgāthā The Verses of the Elder Nun Mittākāḷī, from the Fifth Chapter (Pañcakanipāta) I was once a courtesan, skilled in the arts of love; I was beautiful, charming, and possessed of great wealth. But when I saw the Blessed One, my heart was filled with joy; Having heard his teaching, I took refuge in him. Then, having abandoned all worldly pleasures, I went forth into homelessness under the Sage. Now, free from lust and dwelling in peace, I have attained the state of an arahant. My former life as a courtesan is now but a memory; I am now a nun, disciplined and pure. Having seen the Dhamma, I have crossed over the flood; I have reached the further shore, free from all bonds. I pay homage to the Teacher, the Fully Enlightened One; To the Dhamma and the Sangha, I too offer my respect. May I never again fall back into the world of rebirth; May I dwell in peace, having realized Nibbāna.
Having gone forth from the home life into homelessness out of faith,
I wandered here and there.
Eager for gain and honor,
having abandoned the supreme goal,
I pursued a base goal.
Having fallen under the power of the defilements,
I did not realize the goal of asceticism;
then a sense of spiritual urgency arose within me.
Seated in my dwelling,
I had entered upon a wrong path,
having fallen under the power of craving.
My life is short,
and old age and disease crush it;
before this body breaks apart, [I must strive].
I have no time for negligence.
Contemplating the arising and passing away of the aggregates as they truly are, I am diligent.
With a liberated mind, I arose;
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
… Thus spoke the elder nun Mittā Kāḷī.
